overall_reason: One UI sans (Segoe UI drawn at 1440, from a -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI" stack; system-ui at 375) sets every role, which fits a product component in Operate mode, so TYP-005 does not apply. The table is drawn at half size: .cp-task-design has transform: scale(0.5), so the declared 14px head, 12px names and 10 to 11px columns render at about 7px, 6px and 5px.

score.reason: T-LADDER fails on a type scale shrunk to roughly 5 to 7px on screen (TYP-135); the sweep's text_floor measured the declared 10 to 11px sizes and does not see the scale transform.

findings.title: Never shrink text to fit or to hide a content problem
findings.evidence: The stylesheet sets '.cp-task-design { width: 600px; transform: scale(0.5) }'. The DOM sizes, 'Project tasks' 14px, task names 12px, owners, dates and status 11px and column heads 10px, therefore render at about 7, 6, 5.5 and 5px (01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png and 01-evidence/tiles/375-00.png: the column heads 'Task', 'Owner', 'Due', 'Status' are barely legible).
findings.before: A 600px table scaled to 300px, every role halved on screen
findings.after: Lay the table out at its real width, or drop columns so it fits 300px with names at 13 to 14px and meta at 12px
findings.why: Halving a table to fit its box puts every word under any readable size; the content needs cutting, not shrinking.

findings.title: Weight steps are clear
findings.evidence: The 17 small elements are all weight 400; names (12px) and the owner, due and status columns (11px) differ by 1px only.
findings.after: Names one clear step above the columns (500 to 600, or a size step)
findings.why: Without a step the eye cannot find the task name first in a four-column row.

strengths: One face and one leading value across the table.
not_investigated: T-MEASURE: no paragraph of 3 or more lines at either width (type table measure.paragraphs = 0)
